reporting-org.narrative: United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East

title.narrative: 2025 Syria Regional Appeal - Syria - Coordination and Management

description.narrative: UNRWA will continue its emergency response in Syria through over 3,500 personnel, the majority of whom are Palestine refugees, fostering strong community ties. Additional specialised international personnel, including experts in humanitarian response, access, cash assistance, resilience and advocacy, will be retained to enhance planning, emergency programme delivery, coordination and oversight of humanitarian interventions. The Agency will strengthen community-based protection and AAP by building local capacity to identify and refer protection cases, ensuring accountable assistance through community engagement and personnel training. Guided by its Framework for AAP and the Core Humanitarian Standard on Quality and Accountability, UNRWA will ensure high-quality assistance via community meetings and capacity-building initiatives. A team of telephone operators will manage queries, feedback and complaints, providing direct responses or referrals, supported by an internal coordination mechanism and a community feedback mechanism e-platform. UNRWA will coordinate and foster partnerships with national and international actors in Syria, including inter-agency mechanisms, and maintain information-sharing arrangements with UNHCR and field offices to monitor cross-border movements and facilitate referrals. In response to Syria’s complex security situation, the Agency will conduct security compliance assessments at 48 installations, support 600 humanitarian field missions, and provide safety, security and risk management training to 220 personnel. UNRWA will also implement environmental sustainability initiatives, including personnel and refugee sensitisation, energy consumption reduction, renewable energy adoption and improved solid waste management.
